title: Security Deposit: Accepted Forms of Non-Cash Security
content:
A Security Deposit is ordinarily met in cash. For the kinds marked below, the company accepts a non-cash instrument for the full required amount in place of cash.

| Security Deposit kind | Surety bond for the full required amount | Irrevocable letter of credit for the full required amount | Written guarantee by another Lakeshore customer with satisfactory history | Guarantee released after (months of satisfactory payment) | Interest paid on non-cash security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | Not accepted | Not accepted | Accepted | 12 | No |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | Not accepted | Not accepted | Not accepted | 0 | No |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | Not accepted | Not accepted | Not accepted | 0 | No |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | Not accepted | Not accepted | Not accepted | 0 | No |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | Accepted | Accepted | Not accepted | 0 | No |
| Large Power Service Deposit | Accepted | Accepted | Not accepted | 0 | No |

## Standards

1. A surety bond or an irrevocable letter of credit is accepted only for the Medium Commercial Service Deposit and the Large Power Service Deposit, and only for the full required amount.
2. A third-party guarantee, given in writing by another Lakeshore customer with satisfactory history, is accepted only for the Residential New Service Deposit, and it is released after 12 months of satisfactory payment. The release figure is 0 for every kind that does not accept guarantees.
3. No interest is paid on non-cash security for any kind: instruments earn nothing.

## Applying the table

| Kind and proposed security (hypothetical) | Accepted in place of cash? |
|---|---|
| Large Power Service Deposit, irrevocable letter of credit for the full required amount | Yes |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit, surety bond for the full required amount | Yes |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit, surety bond | No |
| Residential New Service Deposit, written guarantee by another Lakeshore customer with satisfactory history | Yes |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit, written guarantee | No |

title: Business Security Deposit: Additional Amount Due and Its Installments
content:
**Clause.** The additional amount due on a business Security Deposit returned to assessed by a recalculation is the required amount recorded on the deposit less the held cash, which is the cash received less the cash refunded, and never below zero. It is paid in the most installments of the deposit's kind, each the additional amount due divided by that count and rounded down to the cent, the last installment carrying the remainder.

The installment paid first is rounded to the cent and never exceeds the additional amount due. After the installment paid first, the rest of the additional amount due is paid in equal installments over the remaining number, each rounded down to the cent, the last carrying the remainder, each due 30 calendar days after the previous one.


## Worked examples (hypothetical deposits)

**Kind allowing 2 installments.** Required amount recorded USD 7757.00; cash received USD 5000.00; nothing refunded. Held cash USD 5000.00. Additional amount due USD 2757.00. Each installment USD 2757.00 divided by 2, which is USD 1378.50; the installment paid first is USD 1378.50 and the second, due 30 calendar days later, is USD 1378.50.

**Odd cent.** Additional amount due USD 2757.01 over 2 installments: USD 1378.505 rounded down to USD 1378.50 for the first; the last carries the remainder, USD 1378.51.

**Kind allowing 1 installment.** Required amount recorded USD 62000.00; cash received USD 52000.00; an excess refund of USD 2000.00 paid earlier. Held cash USD 50000.00. Additional amount due USD 12000.00, paid as one installment of USD 12000.00.

**Required amount below the held cash.** Required amount recorded USD 4000.00 and held cash USD 4200.00: the additional amount due is zero, never a negative figure.

title: Business Security Deposit: Paying an Additional Deposit
content:
An additional deposit owed after a recalculation raised the requirement of a business Security Deposit is paid by the customer directly to the deposit, in installments numbered on from the deposit's latest installment number, so that no installment number is recorded twice on the deposit.

**Condition on the deposit record.** The installment of an additional deposit is worked out only after the deposit shows its raised required amount and has returned to assessed status.

Stated the other way: while the deposit still shows its earlier required amount, or still stands in held status, the installment of an additional deposit is not worked out.

**Raised requirement and due period.** When a recalculated amount exceeds the held cash by more than the kind's increase threshold of the held cash, the deposit returns to assessed with the raised required amount, and the difference due within the kind's additional-deposit period is the additional amount due on the deposit.

## Installment numbering (hypothetical deposits)

| Latest installment number on the deposit | Numbers of the additional installments |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2, 3, ... |
| 2 | 3, 4, ... |
| 3 | 4, 5, ... |

## Paying the installment: `pay_additional_deposit_64b1dc0d`

**Capability.** The tool pays, as the customer, an installment of the additional amount owed on a business Security Deposit whose requirement was raised. It books a cash deposit payment received today on the deposit under the stated installment number, records on the deposit the number of installments in which the additional amount is being paid, and raises the cash and interest held on the deposit by the amount paid. The payment then appears among the deposit's transactions, and the deposit shows the installment count and the new held amount.

**How it is invoked.** It is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `deposit_id` | The deposit reference number of the deposit being paid, as given to the customer from the security-deposit lookup | Reference number |
| `installment_number` | The installment number this payment satisfies on the deposit | Integer counting from 1 for the deposit's earliest installment |
| `installment_count` | The number of installments in which the additional amount is being paid | Positive integer |
| `amount` | The amount paid | USD with 2 decimal places, a positive amount rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A one-line text receipt naming the new deposit transaction reference number, the installment number and the installment count, the amount received in USD with 2 decimal places, the deposit and the resulting held amount; the transaction reference number in the receipt confirms the payment was received.

title: Number of Installments for an Additional Business Security Deposit
content:
**Credit department schedule.** The number of installments of the additional amount due on a business Security Deposit follows its size, measured against the held cash, which is the cash received on the deposit less the cash refunded from it.

1. Where the additional amount due is at least the held cash and no payment reversal was posted on the secured Electric Service Agreement in the 12 months ending on the payment date, the number is the kind's most installments plus 2.
2. Where it is at least 0.5 (one half) of the held cash but less than the held cash, with no such reversal, the number is the kind's most installments plus 1.
3. Otherwise the number is the kind's most installments.

## Numbers by kind

| Security Deposit kind | Most installments | At least the held cash, no reversal | Half the held cash or more but less than it, no reversal | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 2 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical Medium Commercial Service Deposit, held cash USD 6000.00, no reversal)

| Additional amount due (USD) | Number of installments |
|---|---|
| 6000.00 | 3 |
| 5999.99 | 2 |
| 3000.00 | 2 |
| 2999.99 | 1 |

With a payment reversal posted on the secured agreement in the 12 months, every row above is 1.

title: Opening Installment by Agreement Stage for a Security Deposit on a New Agreement
content:
The opening installment of a Security Deposit on a new agreement follows the stage of the Electric Service Agreement it secures, as the agreement's status and bills show on the payment date.

| Agreement stage | Deposit spread over more than one installment | Opening installment |
|---|---|---|
| Still pending start | Yes | The average monthly bill recorded on the deposit plus an equal share, over the number of installments, of the required amount less that bill, rounded down to the cent |
| Started, with no regular bill yet | Yes | One half of the required amount, rounded down to the cent |
| Any other stage, or a single installment | Either | The required amount divided by the number of installments, rounded down to the cent |

## Cases (hypothetical deposit: required amount USD 620.00, average monthly bill recorded USD 310.00, 3 installments)

| Agreement stage | Opening installment (USD) |
|---|---|
| Pending start | 310.00 plus one third of 310.00, that is 413.333..., rounded down to 413.33 |
| Active, no regular bill issued yet | 310.00 |
| Active, regular bills already issued | 206.66 |

**Single installment.** Where the deposit is paid in one installment, the opening installment is the required amount itself, whatever the stage.

title: Security Deposit Amount Table by Deposit Kind
content:
The amount of a Security Deposit rests on the average monthly bill of the service agreement, a multiple set for each deposit kind, and a minimum and maximum set for each kind. The table below gives those figures for every kind.

| Security Deposit kind | Multiple of the average monthly bill | Regular bills averaged (most recent) | Fewest regular bills at the address for the actual average to be used | Default average monthly bill (USD) | Minimum deposit (USD) | Maximum deposit (USD) | Rounding of the computed deposit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 2.0 | 12 | 6 | 142.00 | 100.00 | 600.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 2.0 | 12 | 6 | 142.00 | 150.00 | 800.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 3.0 | 12 | 6 | 142.00 | 300.00 | 1500.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 2.0 | 12 | 3 | 310.00 | 250.00 | 5000.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 2.5 | 12 | 3 | 2400.00 | 1000.00 | 50000.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 2.0 | 12 | 3 | 41500.00 | 10000.00 | 500000.00 | Rounded up to the next whole dollar |

## Meaning of each column

- **Multiple of the average monthly bill**: the required deposit expressed as a multiple of the average monthly bill.
- **Regular bills averaged**: the number of most recent regular bills averaged to obtain the average monthly bill.
- **Fewest regular bills**: the fewest regular bills at the service address for the actual average to be used; with fewer, the default average monthly bill applies.
- **Default average monthly bill**: the average monthly bill used when the address has too little bill history.
- **Minimum deposit**: the smallest deposit required when a deposit applies.
- **Maximum deposit**: the largest deposit that may be required.

## Illustrations (hypothetical agreements)

- A hypothetical Schedule GD agreement with only 2 regular bills at its address has fewer than the 3 the Medium Commercial Service Deposit calls for, so the default average monthly bill of USD 2400.00 is the average used.
- A hypothetical Schedule RS agreement with 9 regular bills at its address has at least the 6 the Residential New Service Deposit calls for, so its actual average is used, taken over its most recent regular bills up to 12.
- The minimum and maximum differ by kind: a Residential Reestablishment Deposit is never required below USD 150.00 nor above USD 800.00, while a Small Commercial Service Deposit runs from USD 250.00 to USD 5000.00.

title: Security Deposit Interest for a Completed Year
content:
**Commission rates.** The Commission sets the deposit interest rate for each calendar year: 3.85% (0.0385) for 2024, 4.02% (0.0402) for 2025 and 4.17% (0.0417), the annual interest rate of every Security Deposit kind, from 2026 on.

**Clause.** The interest for a completed year of a cash Security Deposit is the cash received on the deposit times the Commission's deposit interest rate for the calendar year of the anniversary, rounded to the cent. The cash received is the total of the deposit payments received on the deposit. The figure is rounded to the cent once, on the final amount.

## Rate by calendar year of the anniversary

| Calendar year in which the anniversary falls | Commission deposit interest rate |
|---|---|
| 2024 | 3.85% |
| 2025 | 4.02% |
| 2026 and later | 4.17% |

## Worked examples (hypothetical deposits)

| Cash received on the deposit (USD) | Anniversary | Rate | Product | Interest credited (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 480.00 | 12 May 2026 | 4.17% | 20.016 | 20.02 |
| 480.00 | 12 May 2025 | 4.02% | 19.296 | 19.30 |
| 1240.00 | 3 November 2024 | 3.85% | 47.74 | 47.74 |

**Which calendar year sets the rate?** The calendar year in which the anniversary closing the year falls.

title: Security Deposit Anniversary Interest Credit
content:
A held cash Security Deposit is credited on each anniversary of its fully secured date with simple interest for the year that the anniversary closes, booked as one interest credit dated that day whose period ends on the anniversary; instruments earn nothing and interest never earns interest.

**Condition on the recorded review date.** The interest for a completed year is credited only once the refund review date recorded on the deposit falls after the anniversary that closes that year.

Put the other way, while the refund review date recorded on the deposit falls on or before that anniversary, the year's interest credit is not booked.

| Refund review date recorded on the deposit, compared with the anniversary closing the year | Year's interest credit booked? |
|---|---|
| Later than the anniversary | Yes |
| The same day as the anniversary | No |
| Earlier than the anniversary | No |

## Booking the credit: `credit_deposit_interest_e2c6de3a`

**Capability.** The tool credits one period of simple interest to a cash Security Deposit. It books an interest credit on the deposit for the period ending on the stated date, dated today, and raises the cash and interest held on the deposit by the amount credited. The credit then appears among the deposit's transactions, and the held amount shown on the deposit includes it.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `deposit_id` | The deposit reference number of the Security Deposit being credited, as returned by the security-deposit lookup for the customer | Reference number |
| `interest_period_end` | The last day of the interest period this credit covers | YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date with no time of day |
| `interest_amount` | The interest credited | USD with 2 decimal places, a positive amount already rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A one-line text receipt naming the new deposit transaction reference number, the deposit, the interest amount credited in USD with 2 decimal places, the period end date and the resulting held amount; the transaction reference number in the receipt confirms the credit was booked.

## Illustration (hypothetical deposit)

A deposit fully secured on 12 May 2025 reaches its first anniversary on 12 May 2026. The credit for that year is booked as one interest credit dated 12 May 2026 with `interest_period_end` 2026-05-12, provided the refund review date recorded on the deposit is later than 12 May 2026.

title: Security Deposit Assessment: Triggers, Timing and Required Amount
content:
**Rule on assessment of a Security Deposit.**

**1. Triggers.** A Security Deposit is assessed only for one of the triggers its kind carries:
(a) a new service agreement opened without a waiver basis;
(b) a disconnection of the agreement for nonpayment;
(c) late payment charges on the agreement in the 12 months before assessment reaching the kind's late payment trigger count, counted as the late payment charges posted on the agreement in the 12 calendar months ending on the assessment date, excluding charges waived by a courtesy late-charge waiver credit;
(d) a confirmed finding of meter tampering or diversion.

**2. Kind.** The deposit kind follows the customer class and the agreement's rate schedule as listed for each kind.

**3. New-service timing.** A new-service deposit must be assessed within the assessment window after the agreement's start date.

**4. Counting.** Each window is counted in calendar days from the day after its triggering date, and an assessment on the last day of the window is in time.

**5. Disconnection date.** The disconnection date is the agreement's last status date while it is disconnected.

**6. Reconnection and energization.** Where the kind requires the first installment before reconnection, a disconnected agreement is not reconnected until the first installment is received; where the kind requires the deposit to be fully secured before energization, a new agreement is not energized until the deposit is held.

**7. Evidence.** Each timing test reads the system record of the triggering date, the agreement's start date, its last status date, the posting date of the late payment charge, or the date of the field investigation, for the agreement, charge or field order concerned, as the records show it before the deposit is assessed.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this rule are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- A deposit triggered by disconnection must be assessed within the assessment window after the disconnection date. (no longer in force)
- A deposit triggered by late payments must be assessed within the assessment window after the posting date of the late payment charge that reached the trigger count. (no longer in force)
- A deposit triggered by unauthorized use must be assessed within the assessment window after the date of the field investigation that confirmed it. (no longer in force)
- The required amount is the kind's multiple times the average monthly bill, rounded up to the next whole dollar, then raised to the kind's minimum deposit and limited to its maximum deposit; the average monthly bill being the mean, rounded to the cent, of the kind's number of most recent regular bills of the agreement before the assessment date, or the kind's default average bill when the agreement has fewer regular bills than the kind requires. (no longer in force)
- The installment count is the kind's most installments, or its most installments when income-qualified where the customer's income qualification runs to or past the assessment date, reduced until each installment reaches the kind's smallest installment. (no longer in force)
- The first installment is due the kind's first-installment days after assessment and later installments under the kind's installment schedule. (no longer in force)

## Boundary cases for the new-service window (hypothetical dates)

For a kind with a 30-day assessment window and an agreement start date of 10 April, the first counted day is 11 April and the last day of the window is 10 May.

| Assessment date | In time? |
|---|---|
| 9 May | Yes |
| 10 May (last day of the window) | Yes |
| 11 May | No |

Expressed generally: an assessment on the last calendar day of the window is in time, and an assessment on the following day is not.

## Points of judgement

- A trigger the kind does not carry does not support an assessment of that kind.
- A late payment charge that was waived by a courtesy late-charge waiver credit does not count toward the late payment trigger count.

title: Autopay Customers: Added Installments on an Additional Business Security Deposit
content:
Autopay lengthens the installment plan of an additional amount owed on a business Security Deposit.

**Rule.** Where at least 6 of the secured Electric Service Agreement's payments posted in the 6 months ending on the payment date came through autopay, 2 installments are added; where at least 3 but fewer than 6 did, 1 is added; otherwise none is added.

| Payments through autopay in the 6 months ending on the payment date | Installments added |
|---|---|
| 6 or more | 2 |
| 3 to 5 | 1 |
| 0 to 2 | None |

Only payments on the secured agreement whose payment channel is autopay are counted.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical counts)

- 6 autopay payments: 2 added; 5 autopay payments: 1 added.
- 3 autopay payments: 1 added; 2 autopay payments: none added.

title: Security Deposit Review Extension: Autopay Reduction
content:
Autopay lowers the extension of the refund review date of a held Security Deposit whose satisfactory payment review is not passed.

**Clause.** Where at least 6 of the secured Electric Service Agreement's payments posted in the 6 months ending on the decision day, the day the review is decided, came through autopay, 2 months come off the extension; where at least 3 but fewer than 6 did, 1 month comes off; otherwise nothing comes off.

## Reduction by autopay payments

| Payments through autopay on the secured agreement in the 6 months ending on the decision day | Months off the extension |
|---|---|
| 6 or more | 2 |
| 3, 4 or 5 | 1 |
| 0, 1 or 2 | Nothing |

The payments counted are those posted on the secured agreement whose payment channel is autopay; payments made by card, online bank transfer, mailed check, pay station or energy assistance agency do not count toward the figure.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical counts)

- 6 autopay payments in the window: 2 months off. With 5, the reduction falls to 1 month.
- 3 autopay payments in the window: 1 month off. With 2, nothing comes off.
- 7 payments in the window, 4 of them through autopay and 3 by card: 4 autopay payments, so 1 month off.

title: Business Security Deposit Recalculation
content:
Held business Security Deposits are subject to recalculation; residential deposits are never recalculated.

## Clauses in force

1. **Lower recalculated amount.** When the recalculated amount is lower than the held cash and the kind refunds excess, the held cash above the new amount is refunded as an excess refund and the deposit stays held.
2. **Residential kinds.** Residential deposits are never recalculated.

## Clauses no longer in force

- Business deposits are recalculated at the kind's recalculation interval after the fully secured date with the same formula as at assessment. (no longer in force; superseded by the current basis)
- When the recalculated amount exceeds the held cash by more than the kind's increase threshold of the held cash, the deposit returns to assessed with the new required amount and the difference due within the kind's additional-deposit period. (no longer in force; superseded by the current basis)

## Hypothetical illustration of an excess refund

A Medium Commercial Service Deposit holds USD 6000.00 in cash and its recalculated amount is USD 5200.00. The kind refunds excess, so USD 800.00 is refunded as an excess refund and the deposit stays held with USD 5200.00 in cash.

## Basis questions

**Is a Residential New Service Deposit recalculated after a year of higher bills?**
No. Residential deposits are never recalculated.

**Does an excess refund change the deposit's status?**
No. The deposit stays held.

title: Business Security Deposit Recalculation Terms
content:
Held Security Deposits of the business kinds are recalculated at a set interval; the residential kinds are not. The terms for each kind are as follows.

| Security Deposit kind | Months between scheduled recalculations of a held deposit | Increase over the held amount that requires an additional deposit (fraction of the held amount) | Held cash above a lower recalculated amount refunded | Additional deposit due (calendar days after it is required) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 0 (never recalculated) | 0 (no increase is required) | No | 0 |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 0 (never recalculated) | 0 (no increase is required) | No | 0 |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 0 (never recalculated) | 0 (no increase is required) | No | 0 |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 24 | 0.25 (25%) | Yes | 10 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 12 | 0.20 (20%) | Yes | 10 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 12 | 0.10 (10%) | Yes | 10 |

## Terms

- **Recalculation interval**: months between scheduled recalculations of the required amount on a held deposit; 0 means the deposit is never recalculated.
- **Increase threshold**: the increase of the recalculated amount over the held amount, as a fraction of the held amount, that triggers an additional deposit; 0 means no increase is required.
- **Excess refunded**: whether held cash above a lower recalculated amount is refunded.
- **Additional deposit due**: the calendar days after an additional deposit is required by which it is due.

## Worked threshold figures (hypothetical held amounts)

| Kind | Hypothetical held amount (USD) | Threshold fraction | Increase above which an additional deposit is triggered (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 800.00 | 0.25 | 200.00 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 6000.00 | 0.20 | 1200.00 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 90000.00 | 0.10 | 9000.00 |

For a hypothetical Medium Commercial Service Deposit required as an additional amount on 4 May, the additional amount is due 10 calendar days later, on 14 May.

title: Business Security Deposit Recalculation and Raised Requirement
content:
A held business Security Deposit is recalculated at the recalculation interval of its kind after its fully secured date, and its recalculated requirement is worked out on the recalculation date.

**Condition on interest credits.** The recalculated requirement is not fixed until the deposit carries an interest credit for every anniversary of its fully secured date reached so far.

Stated the other way: while any anniversary of the fully secured date reached by the recalculation date has no interest credit on the deposit whose period ends on that anniversary, the recalculated requirement is not fixed.

| Anniversaries of the fully secured date reached so far | Interest credits on the deposit with those period ends | Recalculated requirement fixed? |
|---|---|---|
| Two | Both | Yes |
| Two | Only the first | No |
| One | None | No |

## Recording a raised requirement: `require_additional_deposit_b541b477`

**Capability.** The tool records a raised requirement on a held business Security Deposit, returning the deposit to assessed status with the new required amount. The deposit's required amount and the average monthly bill behind it are replaced by the stated values, the date the additional amount falls due is recorded, the deposit's status becomes assessed, and today becomes both its assessment date and its status date. The cash already held stays on the deposit. The new requirement and due date show on the deposit at once.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `deposit_id` | The deposit reference number of the held deposit whose requirement is raised, as returned by the security-deposit lookup for the customer | Reference number |
| `required_amount` | The new required deposit amount | USD with 2 decimal places, a whole-dollar amount written with .00 cents |
| `average_monthly_bill` | The average monthly bill the new requirement rests on | USD with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |
| `due_date` | The date by which the additional amount is due | YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date with no time of day |

**Return.** A one-line text receipt naming the deposit, its new required amount and average monthly bill in USD with 2 decimal places, its status (assessed) and the due date; the assessed status in the receipt confirms the raised requirement was recorded.

title: Security Deposit Anniversary Interest Across Two Calendar Years
content:
**Rule on the rate earned over the year being credited on a Security Deposit anniversary.**

The year being credited begins on the period end of the latest interest credit on the deposit, or on the fully secured date when no interest has been credited yet, and ends on the anniversary, covering the 12 months ending on it. The closing year's rate is the Commission rate of the calendar year of the anniversary: 3.85% (0.0385) for 2024, 4.02% (0.0402) for 2025 and 4.17% (0.0417) for 2026 on, the last being the annual interest rate of every Security Deposit kind. Days are counted from the start date to the end date, the start date not counted.

1. Where the year being credited began in an earlier calendar year than its anniversary and that earlier year's rate differs from the closing year's rate, its days up to and including 31 December of that earlier year earn the earlier year's rate and its days from 1 January of the anniversary's year on earn the closing year's rate, each counted as days over 365.
2. Where the period credited is shorter than 365 days and earns a single year's rate, its days earn the closing year's rate as days over 365.
3. Otherwise the whole year earns the closing year's rate.

## Worked cases (hypothetical periods)

**Period from 12 May 2025 to 12 May 2026.** It began in 2025 (rate 4.02%) and closes in 2026 (rate 4.17%); the rates differ, so clause 1 applies. Days from 13 May to 31 December 2025: 233. Days from 1 January to 12 May 2026: 132. Rate earned over the period: 233 days times 4.02% plus 132 days times 4.17%, over 365, which is 1487.10 percentage-days over 365, about 4.0742%.

**Period from 20 February 2026 to 12 May 2026.** It lies within one calendar year, so a single rate applies, and it is 81 days long, shorter than 365. Clause 2 applies: 81 days over 365 at 4.17%.

**Period from 1 August 2026 to 1 August 2027.** Both calendar years carry 4.17%, so no split arises, and the period is 365 days. Clause 3 applies: the whole year earns 4.17%.

| Began in an earlier calendar year with a different rate | Shorter than 365 days | Rate earned |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | Split by days at each year's rate, days over 365 |
| No | Yes | Closing year's rate times days over 365 |
| No | No | Closing year's rate for the whole year |

title: Clean Payment Months Credited Against a Security Deposit Review Extension
content:
**Questions and answers for customer care on clean payment earned before a Security Deposit review is decided.**

**What is credited?**
Clean payment already earned since the latest lapse is credited against the length of the extension of the refund review date of a held Security Deposit whose satisfactory payment review is not passed; the credited months come off the extension.

**How many months are credited?**

| Situation on the decision day (the day the review is decided) | Months credited |
|---|---|
| The latest late payment charge posted on the secured Electric Service Agreement, waived or not, lies at least 3 whole months before the decision day, and no disconnection is counted | The whole months from that charge's posting date to the decision day |
| A disconnection is counted | The whole months from the posting date of the customer's latest reconnection charge to the decision day |
| Any other situation | None |

**When is a disconnection counted?**
When a reconnection charge was posted on any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements in the review window, which is the kind's review months ending on the decision day, or when any of the customer's agreements is disconnected on the decision day. The review months are 12 for the Residential New Service Deposit and the Residential Reestablishment Deposit, 24 for the Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit, the Small Commercial Service Deposit and the Medium Commercial Service Deposit, and 36 for the Large Power Service Deposit.

**How are whole months counted?**
From the earlier date to the same day of a later month, a month whose day has not yet been reached on the later date not counting.

**Does a late payment charge that was later waived still mark the latest lapse?**
Yes. The latest late payment charge is taken waived or not.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

| Latest late payment charge | Latest reconnection charge | Disconnection counted | Decision day | Whole months | Months credited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 January | none | No | 9 June | 4 | 4 |
| 9 March | none | No | 9 June | 3 | 3 |
| 10 March | none | No | 9 June | 2 | None (fewer than 3) |
| 5 May | 20 February | Yes | 5 June | 3 from the reconnection charge | 3 |

title: Security Deposit at Closing and on a Move: Terms by Kind
content:
**Terms for customers who move or close an Electric Service account.** Whether a held Security Deposit follows the customer to a new service agreement, and the order in which a deposit applied at closing meets what is owed, are set for each kind as follows.

| Security Deposit kind | Held deposit moves with the customer to a new service agreement | Order in which a deposit applied at closing meets the final balance |
|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | Yes | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | Yes | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | Yes | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | No | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | No | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |
| Large Power Service Deposit | No | Final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the customer, remainder refunded |

## Conditions

1. A held deposit of the three residential kinds moves with the customer to the customer's new service agreement; a held deposit of the three business kinds does not.
2. For every kind, a deposit applied at closing meets the closing agreement's final bill first, then any other closed-agreement balance of the same customer, and only the remainder is refunded.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A hypothetical Small Commercial Service Deposit of USD 900.00 with interest is applied when its agreement closes. The final bill is USD 620.00 and another closed agreement of the same customer carries an unpaid balance of USD 180.00. The deposit meets the USD 620.00 final bill, then the USD 180.00 balance, and the remaining USD 100.00 is refunded.

title: Closing Period of a Security Deposit Refund: Cash Earning Interest
content:
The cash on which a Security Deposit earns interest within a refund, for the closing period, depends on the refunds and payments among the deposit's transactions. The closing period runs from the period end of the latest interest credit on the deposit, or from the fully secured date when none has been credited, to the refund date.

| Deposit's transactions | Interest within the refund is earned on |
|---|---|
| An excess refund has been paid out of the deposit, and no deposit payment was received in the closing period | The cash received less the excess refunds paid |
| A deposit payment was received in the closing period | The cash held when the closing period began plus one half of the payments received in it |
| Neither | The cash received |

The cash received is the total of the deposit payments received on the deposit; an excess refund is a refund paid out of a held deposit after a recalculation lowered its required amount.

## Cases (hypothetical deposits)

1. Payments received USD 9000.00, all before the closing period; excess refund of USD 1500.00 paid earlier. Interest is earned on USD 7500.00.
2. Cash held USD 2000.00 when the closing period began, nothing refunded, and a USD 600.00 payment received during the period. Interest is earned on USD 2000.00 plus USD 300.00, that is USD 2300.00.
3. Payments received USD 480.00, nothing refunded and no payment in the closing period. Interest is earned on USD 480.00.

title: Months Earned in the Closing Period of a Security Deposit Refund
content:
The closing period of a Security Deposit refund earns interest only for months of satisfactory payment on the secured Electric Service Agreement. A closing period that earns fewer than 12 months is paid interest for those months only, out of the 12 months of a full year.

**Lapse months.** The lapses of the closing period are those of the 12 months ending on the refund date. Late payment charges on the secured Electric Service Agreement are counted after deducting one for each courtesy late-charge waiver credit.

| In the lapse months | Months earned |
|---|---|
| A reconnection charge was posted on any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements, or a payment reversal was posted on the secured agreement, or 3 or more late payment charges are counted | 6 |
| 1 or more but fewer than 3 late payment charges are counted, with no payment reversal and no reconnection charge | 9 |
| Otherwise | 12 |

## Truth table (hypothetical 12-month records)

| Late payment charges posted | Courtesy waiver credits | Counted | Payment reversal | Reconnection charge on any agreement | Months earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | No | No | 12 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | No | No | 9 |
| 3 | 1 | 2 | No | No | 9 |
| 4 | 1 | 3 | No | No | 6 |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | Yes | No | 6 |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | No | Yes | 6 |

title: Closing Period of a Security Deposit Refund: Opening Rate
content:
**Closing period.** The closing period of a Security Deposit refund runs from the period end of the latest interest credit on the deposit, or from the fully secured date when none has been credited, to the refund date.

**Opening rate.** The closing period's opening rate is 4.02% (0.0402) when the period began in 2025, 3.85% (0.0385) when it began in 2024, and 4.17% (0.0417), the annual interest rate of every Security Deposit kind, otherwise.

| Closing period began in | Opening rate |
|---|---|
| Calendar 2025 | 4.02% |
| Calendar 2024 | 3.85% |
| Any other calendar year | 4.17% |

## Cases (hypothetical deposits)

| Deposit record | Closing period began | Opening rate |
|---|---|---|
| Latest interest credit with period end 18 November 2025 | 18 November 2025 | 4.02% |
| No interest credit; fully secured on 2 September 2024 | 2 September 2024 | 3.85% |
| Latest interest credit with period end 6 March 2026 | 6 March 2026 | 4.17% |

title: Rate Earned Over the Closing Period of a Security Deposit Refund
content:
**Rule on the interest rate earned within a refund, for the closing period.**

The closing period runs from the period end of the latest interest credit on the Security Deposit, or from the fully secured date when none has been credited, to the refund date. Its days are counted from its start date to the refund date, the start date not counted. Its closing rate is the Commission rate of the calendar year of the refund date: 3.85% (0.0385) for 2024, 4.02% (0.0402) for 2025 and 4.17% (0.0417) for 2026 onward. The time the deposit has been held is counted in whole months from its fully secured date to the refund date.

1. Where the deposit has been held at least the kind's minimum holding months on the refund date, and the closing period began in an earlier calendar year than the refund date with an opening rate that differs from its closing rate, its days up to and including 31 December of that earlier year earn the opening rate and its days from 1 January of the refund date's year on earn the closing rate, each as days over 365.
2. Where the deposit has been held fewer than the kind's minimum holding months on the refund date, the closing period earns no interest.
3. Otherwise the days of the closing period earn the closing rate as days over 365.

## Minimum holding months by kind

| Security Deposit kind | Minimum holding months |
|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 6 |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 6 |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 6 |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 6 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 6 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 6 |

## Cases (hypothetical deposits)

**Held 9 months; closing period 12 May 2025 to 12 February 2026; opening rate 4.02%, closing rate 4.17%.** Clause 1 applies: 233 days (13 May to 31 December 2025) at 4.02% and 43 days (1 January to 12 February 2026) at 4.17%, each over 365: 1115.97 percentage-days over 365, about 3.0575% for the period.

**Held 4 months.** Clause 2 applies: the closing period earns no interest.

**Held 18 months; closing period 1 March 2026 to 30 June 2026.** One calendar year, so clause 3 applies: 121 days over 365 at 4.17%.

title: Security Deposit Application to the Final Bill and Cancelled Start Orders
content:
**Closing of the secured agreement.** When the secured service agreement closes, a Security Deposit in held or assessed status is applied to its final balance on the final bill date, together with interest earned through that date, in the order of application set for its kind.

**Moving customers.** A deposit whose kind allows transfer on a move, and whose customer has opened a new service agreement before the closure, is moved instead of applied.

**Cancelled start orders.** When a start order is cancelled before the service began, the deposit is cancelled and any cash received is refunded in full.

**Posting of the application.** An application is posted only on a deposit in applied to final bill status, as the deposit record shows it.

## Outcome table at closing

| Deposit status at closing | Kind allows transfer and the customer opened a new agreement before the closure | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Held | No | Applied to the final balance on the final bill date, with interest earned through that date |
| Assessed | No | Applied to the final balance on the final bill date |
| Held | Yes | Moved instead of applied |

## Hypothetical illustrations

1. A Residential Reestablishment Deposit is held when the customer closes the agreement without opening another. The deposit, with interest earned through the final bill date, is applied to the final balance on the final bill date.
2. A customer's start order is cancelled before service began, after the customer had paid a USD 40.00 first installment on a Residential New Service Deposit. The deposit is cancelled and the USD 40.00 is refunded in full.

title: Credited Interest Counted Toward a Raised Business Security Deposit
content:
Credited interest counts toward a raised requirement on a long-held business Security Deposit. The figure that stands against the required amount recorded on the deposit, when the additional amount due is worked out, is the deposit's held basis.

**Held basis.** Held cash is the cash received on the deposit less the cash refunded from it. Whole months are counted from the fully secured date to the payment date, from the earlier date to the same day of a later month, a month whose day has not yet been reached on the later date not counting. Payment reversals are those posted on the secured Electric Service Agreement in the 24 months ending on the payment date.

| Time fully secured on the payment date | Payment reversal on the secured agreement in the 24 months | Held basis |
|---|---|---|
| At least 24 whole months | None | Held cash plus all interest credited on the deposit |
| At least 12 but fewer than 24 whole months | None | Held cash plus one half of the interest credited on the deposit |
| Any other case | Any | Held cash alone |

**Becoming held again.** A deposit becomes held on the day the cash received on it reaches its required amount, or on the day an accepted instrument for the full required amount is lodged, except that a deposit returned to assessed by a recalculation becomes held again on the day its held basis reaches the raised required amount, or on the day an accepted instrument for the full raised required amount is lodged.

## Cases (hypothetical deposit: held cash USD 5000.00, interest credited USD 300.00)

| Fully secured date | Payment date | Whole months | Reversal in the 24 months | Held basis (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March 2024 | 10 March 2026 | 24 | None | 5300.00 |
| 10 March 2024 | 9 March 2026 | 23 | None | 5150.00 |
| 10 March 2025 | 9 March 2026 | 11 | None | 5000.00 |
| 10 March 2024 | 10 March 2026 | 24 | One | 5000.00 |

title: Customer Payment Record and the New Agreement Security Deposit Multiple
content:
**Credit rule for new agreements.** The multiple for a Security Deposit on a new agreement follows the customer's payment record on all its Electric Service Agreements in the 12 months ending on the assessment date, late payment charges being counted after deducting one for each courtesy late-charge waiver credit.

1. Where no late payment charge is counted and no payment reversal was posted, the multiple is the kind's deposit multiple less 0.5.
2. Where 2 or more late payment charges are counted or any payment reversal was posted, it is the kind's deposit multiple plus 0.5.
3. Otherwise it is the kind's deposit multiple.

## Multiples by kind

| Security Deposit kind | Kind's deposit multiple | Clean record | 2 or more counted, or a reversal | Otherwise (exactly 1 counted, no reversal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 2.0 | 1.5 | 2.5 | 2.0 |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 2.0 | 1.5 | 2.5 | 2.0 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 2.5 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 2.5 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 2.0 | 1.5 | 2.5 | 2.0 |

## Truth table (hypothetical records across all of the customer's agreements)

| Late payment charges posted | Courtesy waiver credits | Counted | Payment reversals | Multiple |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Less 0.5 |
| 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | Less 0.5 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | Kind's multiple |
| 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 | Plus 0.5 |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | Plus 0.5 |

title: Security Deposit Credit History Judged Across the Customer
content:
For every Security Deposit, credit history is judged across the customer, not only the secured service agreement. Three rules follow from this.

1. **Disconnections count against every deposit.** A disconnection for nonpayment on any of the customer's service agreements during the review period counts against the refund of every deposit the customer holds. Disconnections in a review period are counted as the reconnection charges posted on any of the customer's service agreements in the period, plus one for each of the customer's agreements currently in disconnected status. The review period is the kind's review months ending on the deposit's refund review date.
2. **Prior Lakeshore history.** The prior Lakeshore history waiver counts any closed agreement of the same customer.
3. **Application at closure.** A deposit applied at closure meets the closing agreement's final balance first, then the unpaid balance of any other closed agreement of the same customer, and only the remainder is refunded.

## Illustrations (hypothetical customer)

A residential customer holds a Residential New Service Deposit on agreement A, whose 12-month review period ends on its refund review date. The customer also has agreement B at a second address.

| Record in A's review period | Disconnections counted against the refund of the deposit on A |
|---|---|
| No reconnection charge on A or B; neither agreement disconnected now | 0 |
| One reconnection charge posted on B; neither agreement disconnected now | 1 |
| No reconnection charge; B currently in disconnected status | 1 |
| One reconnection charge posted on A and B currently disconnected | 2 |

If, hypothetically, the deposit on A is instead applied when A closes, and closed agreement C of the same customer still carries an unpaid balance, the deposit meets A's final balance first, then C's unpaid balance, and only what remains is refunded.

title: Disconnection Notices and the Security Deposit Review Extension
content:
**Collections rule for held Security Deposits whose satisfactory payment review is not passed.** Disconnection notices issued on the secured Electric Service Agreement in the review window add to the extension of the refund review date.

The review window is the kind's review months ending on the decision day, the day on which the review is decided: 12 months for the Residential New Service Deposit and the Residential Reestablishment Deposit, 24 months for the Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit, the Small Commercial Service Deposit and the Medium Commercial Service Deposit, and 36 months for the Large Power Service Deposit.

| Disconnection notices issued on the secured agreement in the window | Months added to the extension |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 3 |
| Exactly one | 1 |
| None | Nothing |

Each disconnection notice on the agreement's record counts as one notice, whether it is a written notice or a final notice. Notices on the customer's other agreements are not counted.

## Cases (hypothetical Small Commercial Service Deposit, 24-month window)

| Notices on the secured agreement in the 24 months ending on the decision day | Months added |
|---|---|
| A written notice and a final notice | 3 |
| One written notice 20 months before the decision day | 1 |
| One written notice 26 months before the decision day | Nothing (outside the window) |
| None on the secured agreement, two on another agreement of the customer | Nothing |

title: Established Locations: Reduction of the New Agreement Security Deposit Multiple
content:
An established sister location lowers the multiple of a Security Deposit on a new agreement still pending start.

**Clause.** Where the estimate of the new agreement's monthly bill is drawn from a sister agreement, the customer's other active Electric Service Agreement on the same rate schedule, that has been in service at least 120 whole months on the assessment date, 0.25 comes off the multiple; where from one in service at least 60 but fewer than 120 whole months, 0.1 comes off; otherwise nothing comes off.

**Counting.** Service length runs from the sister agreement's start date to the assessment date. Whole months between two dates are counted from the earlier date to the same day of a later month, a month whose day has not yet been reached on the later date not counting.

| Estimate source | Sister agreement's whole months in service | Taken off the multiple |
|---|---|---|
| Sister agreement | 120 or more | 0.25 |
| Sister agreement | 60 to 119 | 0.1 |
| Sister agreement | Fewer than 60 | Nothing |
| The kind's default average monthly bill | Not applicable | Nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Sister agreement start date | Assessment date | Whole months | Taken off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 April 2016 | 5 April 2026 | 120 | 0.25 |
| 5 April 2016 | 4 April 2026 | 119 | 0.1 |
| 5 April 2021 | 4 April 2026 | 59 | Nothing |

title: Front-Loaded First Installment on an Additional Business Security Deposit
content:
The installment paid first on an additional amount owed on a business Security Deposit is front-loaded on a weak record when the amount is spread.

**Regular installment.** The additional amount due divided by the number of installments of the plan, rounded down to the cent.

**Rule.** Records are read on the secured Electric Service Agreement for the 12 months ending on the payment date.

| Record in the 12 months | Plan has more than one installment | Installment paid first |
|---|---|---|
| A disconnection notice was issued on the secured agreement | Yes | 2 times the regular installment |
| No disconnection notice, and at least one late payment charge is counted after deducting one for each courtesy late-charge waiver credit | Yes | 1.5 times the regular installment |
| Any other record, or a plan of one installment | Either | The regular installment |

## Cases (hypothetical plan: regular installment USD 700.00 over 4 installments)

| Notices in the 12 months | Late payment charges posted | Courtesy waiver credits | Installment paid first (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 1400.00 |
| 0 | 2 | 1 | 1050.00 |
| 0 | 1 | 1 | 700.00 |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 700.00 |

For a plan of one installment, the installment paid first is the regular installment whatever the record shows.

title: Good-Payment Relief on a New Agreement Security Deposit
content:
A Security Deposit of the same kind recently returned for good payment lowers the multiple of a Security Deposit on a new agreement.

**Rule.** The deposit considered is the customer's deposit of that kind on the sister agreement, the customer's other active Electric Service Agreement on the new agreement's rate schedule.

| That deposit's record | Taken off the multiple |
|---|---|
| Refunded in full in the 12 months ending on the assessment date | 0.5 |
| Still held, and fully secured for at least 24 whole months on the assessment date | 0.25 |
| Otherwise | Nothing |

A full refund is shown among the deposit's transactions as a refund of the whole deposit. Whole months are counted from the fully secured date to the assessment date, from the earlier date to the same day of a later month, a month whose day has not yet been reached on the later date not counting.

## Cases (hypothetical assessment date 15 June 2026)

| Deposit of the same kind on the sister agreement | Taken off |
|---|---|
| Refunded in full on 2 March 2026 | 0.5 |
| Refunded in full on 10 June 2025 | Nothing (more than 12 months before) |
| Held, fully secured on 15 June 2024 (24 whole months) | 0.25 |
| Held, fully secured on 16 June 2024 (23 whole months) | Nothing |
| Assessed, never fully secured | Nothing |

title: Security Deposit Installment Terms
content:
**Terms for customers paying a Security Deposit in cash installments.** Lakeshore Power & Light Company allows a cash Security Deposit to be paid in installments up to the number set for its kind. The terms for each kind are as follows.

| Security Deposit kind | Most installments | Most installments when the customer's income qualification is current at assessment | Smallest installment (USD) | First installment due (calendar days after assessment) | Later installments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 3 | 3 | 25.00 | 21 | Each later installment due 30 calendar days after the previous one |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 2 | 6 | 25.00 | 0 | Each later installment due 30 calendar days after the previous one |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 1 | 2 | 25.00 | 0 | Each later installment due 30 calendar days after the previous one |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 2 | 2 | 100.00 | 10 | Each later installment due 30 calendar days after the previous one |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 1 | 1 | 100.00 | 10 | Single payment |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 1 | 1 | 100.00 | 10 | Single payment |

## Conditions

1. **Most installments** is the largest number of installments in which the deposit of that kind may be paid.
2. **Most installments when income-qualified** is the largest number when the customer's income qualification is current at assessment.
3. **Smallest installment** is the lowest amount any installment may be; the installment count is reduced until each installment reaches it.
4. **First installment due** is counted in calendar days after the assessment date; a figure of 0 means the first installment is due on the assessment date itself.

## Questions on these terms

**May a Large Power Service Deposit be spread over several installments?**
Not under this table: its most installments figure is 1 and its later-installment term is a single payment.

**When is the first installment of a Residential Reestablishment Deposit due?**
On the assessment date, since its figure is 0 days.

**When is the first installment of a Residential New Service Deposit due if, hypothetically, the deposit is assessed on 1 March?**
Twenty-one calendar days after assessment, which is 22 March.

**What does the income-qualified column change for a Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit?**
It allows up to 2 installments instead of 1 when the customer's income qualification is current at assessment.

title: Security Deposit Anniversary Interest: Cash on Which Interest Is Earned
content:
The cash on which a Security Deposit earns interest for the year credited on its anniversary depends on the refunds and payments shown among the deposit's transactions.

| Deposit's transactions | Interest is earned on |
|---|---|
| An excess refund has been paid out of the deposit, and no deposit payment was received in the year being credited | The cash received less the excess refunds paid |
| A deposit payment was received in the year being credited | The cash held when the year began plus one half of the payments received in the year |
| Neither of the above | The cash received |

**Terms.** The cash received is the total of the deposit payments received on the deposit. An excess refund is a refund paid out of a held deposit after a recalculation lowered its required amount. The payments of the year being credited are counted over the 12 months ending on the day the credit is booked, which is the anniversary.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A deposit has received USD 6000.00 in payments, an excess refund of USD 800.00 was paid out of it, and no payment was received in the 12 months ending on the anniversary. Interest is earned on USD 5200.00.
2. A deposit held USD 1000.00 in cash when the year began, with no refunds, and received a further USD 400.00 payment during the year. Interest is earned on USD 1000.00 plus one half of USD 400.00, that is USD 1200.00.
3. A deposit has received USD 480.00 in payments, all before the year began, and nothing has been refunded. Interest is earned on USD 480.00.

title: Security Deposit Interest: Holding Period and Crediting Status
content:
Interest on a cash Security Deposit is governed by the following clauses.

## Clauses in force

1. **Minimum holding.** No interest is paid when the deposit has been held for less than the kind's minimum holding months in total.
2. **Once per period, held deposits only.** Each interest period is credited once, and interest is credited only on a deposit in held status, as the deposit record shows its status.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- Cash deposits earn simple interest at the kind's annual rate from the fully secured date; instruments earn nothing. (no longer in force)
- Interest for a full year is credited on each anniversary of the fully secured date, and for a part year it is credited pro rata by days held over 365 on the refund or application date, rounded to the cent. (no longer in force)
- Interest is never compounded: it is computed on the cash received, excluding earlier interest. (no longer in force)

## Status table for interest crediting

| Deposit status | Interest credited? |
|---|---|
| Held | Yes, once per interest period |
| Assessed | No |
| Waived | No |
| Refunded | No |
| Applied to final bill | No |
| Cancelled | No |

## Basis questions

**Is interest paid on a cash deposit held only 4 months in total, where the kind's minimum holding period is 6 months (hypothetical)?**
No. The deposit has been held less than the minimum holding months.

**May the same interest period be credited a second time?**
No. Each interest period is credited once.

title: Security Deposit Interest Rate and Crediting Terms
content:
Cash held as a Security Deposit earns simple interest at the annual rate set by the Commission for the year. The rate, the crediting term and the holding period are the same for every kind.

| Security Deposit kind | Simple annual interest rate on cash deposits | When interest is credited | Months a cash deposit must be held before any interest is paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Simple interest credited to the deposit on each anniversary of the fully secured date, and pro rata to the day at refund or application | 6 |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Same as above | 6 |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Same as above | 6 |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Same as above | 6 |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Same as above | 6 |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 4.17% (0.0417) | Same as above | 6 |

## Notes

- The rate is a simple annual rate expressed as a decimal fraction (0.0417) or a percentage (4.17%); it is the rate the Commission sets for the year.
- The holding term is a count of months: a cash deposit must have been held 6 months before any interest is paid on it.
- The crediting term ties full-year crediting to the anniversary of the date the Security Deposit became fully secured, and part-year crediting to the day of refund or application.

## Questions on this schedule

**Does a business Security Deposit earn a different rate from a residential one?**
No. Every kind in the schedule shows the same rate, 4.17%.

**Is the holding term counted from the assessment date?**
The schedule counts months the cash deposit has been held, and the crediting term counts anniversaries from the fully secured date, not from the assessment date.

title: Security Deposit Kinds, Rate Schedules and Triggering Events
content:
Lakeshore Power & Light Company assesses a Security Deposit under one of six kinds. The kind follows the customer class of record and the rate schedule of the service agreement, and each kind is assessed only on the triggering events marked for it below.

## Schedule of kinds

| Security Deposit kind | Customer class | Rate schedules | Residential agreements only |
|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | Residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | Yes |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | Residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | Yes |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | Residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | Yes |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | Business | Schedules GS and GST | No |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | Business | Schedule GD | No |
| Large Power Service Deposit | Business | Schedule LP | No |

## Triggering events and timing terms

| Security Deposit kind | New agreement opened without a waiver basis | Disconnection for nonpayment of the agreement | Late payment charges within 12 months that allow a deposit on an existing agreement | Confirmed meter tampering or diversion finding required | Assessment window (calendar days after the triggering event) | Deposit fully secured before a new agreement is energized | First installment received before a disconnected agreement is reconnected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | Triggers | Does not trigger | 0 | No | 30 | No | No |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | Does not trigger | Triggers | 3 | No | 30 | No | Yes |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | Does not trigger | Does not trigger | 0 | Yes | 60 | No | Yes |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | Triggers | Triggers | 2 | No | 30 | No | Yes |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | Triggers | Triggers | 2 | No | 30 | No | Yes |
| Large Power Service Deposit | Triggers | Triggers | 2 | No | 30 | Yes | Yes |

Notes to the schedule:

1. A late payment count of 0 means late payments are not a trigger for that kind.
2. The assessment window is the number of calendar days after the triggering event within which the deposit may be assessed.
3. "Fully secured before energization" states whether the Security Deposit must be fully secured before a new service agreement of that kind is energized.
4. "First installment before reconnection" states whether the first installment must be paid before a disconnected agreement of that kind is reconnected.

## Reading the schedule

- **A residential agreement on Schedule RT that has been disconnected for nonpayment** falls under the Residential Reestablishment Deposit, the only residential kind for which disconnection is a triggering event.
- **A residential agreement with late payment charges** can be assessed only under the Residential Reestablishment Deposit, at a count of 3; the other two residential kinds show 0.
- **A business agreement on Schedule GD** falls under the Medium Commercial Service Deposit; a new agreement, a disconnection for nonpayment or a count of 2 late payment charges within 12 months are each a triggering event for it.
- **The Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit** has the longest assessment window, 60 calendar days, and is assessed only on a confirmed tampering or diversion finding.
- **Only the Large Power Service Deposit** must be fully secured before a new agreement is energized.

title: Phasing In a Business Security Deposit Rise from Load Growth
content:
A rise in the requirement of a held business Security Deposit driven by recent load growth is phased in against the held amount.

**Held amount.** The cash received on the deposit less the cash refunded from it, plus the interest credited on the deposit.

**Rule.** Where the billing basis of the recalculation is the recent mean (the mean of the regular bills issued in the 3 months ending on the recalculation date):
- if the requirement before rounding exceeds the held amount by more than 1 times the held amount, only 0.5 (one half) of that excess is added to the held amount;
- if the requirement before rounding exceeds the held amount by no more than 1 times it, 0.75 (three quarters) of the excess is added.

Otherwise the requirement before rounding is taken in full.

| Billing basis is the recent mean | Excess of the requirement before rounding over the held amount | Phased amount |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | More than the held amount | Held amount plus one half of the excess |
| Yes | Above zero, up to the held amount | Held amount plus three quarters of the excess |
| Yes | None | Requirement before rounding |
| No | Any | Requirement before rounding |

## Cases (hypothetical deposit: cash received USD 3900.00, nothing refunded, interest credited USD 100.00, so a held amount of USD 4000.00)

| Basis is the recent mean | Requirement before rounding (USD) | Excess (USD) | Phased amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | 9000.00 | 5000.00 (more than 4000.00) | 4000.00 plus 2500.00, which is 6500.00 |
| Yes | 7000.00 | 3000.00 | 4000.00 plus 2250.00, which is 6250.00 |
| No | 7000.00 | 3000.00 | 7000.00 |

title: Months of Interest Earned on a Security Deposit Anniversary
content:
Interest on a Security Deposit is earned only for months of satisfactory payment on the secured Electric Service Agreement. A year that earns fewer than 12 months of interest is credited for those months only, out of the 12 months of a full year.

**Counting.** The payments and lapses of the year being credited are counted over the 12 months ending on the day the credit is booked, which is the anniversary. Late payment charges on the secured Electric Service Agreement are counted after deducting one for each courtesy late-charge waiver credit posted in the year.

| In the year being credited | Months of interest earned |
|---|---|
| A reconnection charge was posted on any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements, or a payment reversal was posted on the secured agreement, or 3 or more late payment charges are counted | 6 |
| 1 or more but fewer than 3 late payment charges are counted, with no payment reversal and no reconnection charge | 9 |
| Otherwise | 12 |

## Truth table (hypothetical years)

| Late payment charges posted | Courtesy waiver credits | Counted | Payment reversal on the secured agreement | Reconnection charge on any agreement | Months earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | No | No | 12 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | No | No | 9 |
| 2 | 0 | 2 | No | No | 9 |
| 3 | 1 | 2 | No | No | 9 |
| 3 | 0 | 3 | No | No | 6 |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | Yes | No | 6 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | No | Yes, on another agreement | 6 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | No | No | 12 |

title: Multi-Site Customers: Added Installments on a New Agreement Security Deposit
content:
An established multi-site customer gets a longer installment plan for a Security Deposit on a new agreement.

**Rule.** Where three or more regular bills were issued on the customer's Electric Service Agreements in the 1 month ending on the payment date, 2 installments are added; where exactly two were, 1 is added; otherwise none is added.

| Regular bills issued on the customer's agreements in the 1 month ending on the payment date | Installments added |
|---|---|
| Three or more | 2 |
| Exactly two | 1 |
| One or none | None |

Only regular bills count; a final bill issued at the closing of an agreement is not a regular bill.

## Cases (hypothetical business customer, payment date 20 May)

- Regular bills issued on three site agreements on 25 April, 2 May and 9 May: three bills in the month, 2 added.
- Regular bills issued on two site agreements in the month, plus a final bill on a third: two regular bills, 1 added.
- One regular bill in the month: none added.

title: Security Deposit on a New Service Agreement: Assessment
content:
A new service agreement that is still pending start and was opened without a waiver basis is assessed a new-service Security Deposit of the kind its customer class and rate schedule call for, within the assessment window after its start date, and the deposit required is worked out on the assessment date.

**Conditions on the customer's other deposits.**

- The deposit required on a new agreement is not fixed until every other deposit of the customer that stands assessed shows its first installment received.
- The deposit required on a new agreement is fixed only after any deposit of the customer whose satisfactory payment review has been passed on its refund review date stands refunded.

| The customer's other deposit, as its record stands | Does it hold up fixing the new agreement's deposit? |
|---|---|
| Assessed, with its first installment shown as received | No |
| Assessed, with no first installment received | Yes |
| Review passed on its refund review date, still standing held | Yes |
| Review passed on its refund review date, standing refunded | No |

**Triggers that stay with their own agreement.** A disconnection, a late payment count or an unauthorized-use finding never triggers a deposit on a new agreement opened after it; the deposit it triggers is assessed on the agreement that carries it, within the assessment window after the disconnection date, after the posting date of the late payment charge that reached the trigger count, or after the date of the field investigation that confirmed the unauthorized use.

**Installments.** The number of installments of a deposit on a new agreement is not set at assessment; it is recorded with the deposit's opening installment.

## Recording the assessment: `assess_new_service_deposit_5e8da269`

**Capability.** The tool assesses a cash Security Deposit on a newly opened service agreement of a customer. It creates a new deposit in assessed status on the stated agreement, dated today, for the reason of new service, to be met in cash, with the stated kind, average monthly bill, required amount and first installment due date; nothing has been received on it yet, and its number of installments is left at zero until an installment is paid. The deposit then shows in the customer's security deposits with its new reference number.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `customer_id`: the customer reference number of the agreement's customer of record, as returned by the customer profile lookup.
- `service_account_id`: the service account number of the newly opened agreement the deposit secures, as returned by the service-agreement lookup for the customer.
- `variant_name`: the deposit kind, one of "Residential New Service Deposit" (a residential agreement on Schedules RS, RT or REV opened without a waiver basis), "Residential Reestablishment Deposit" (a residential agreement disconnected for nonpayment or with a late payment history), "Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit" (a residential agreement with confirmed meter tampering or diversion), "Small Commercial Service Deposit" (a business agreement on Schedules GS or GST), "Medium Commercial Service Deposit" (a business agreement on Schedule GD) or "Large Power Service Deposit" (a business agreement on Schedule LP).
- `average_monthly_bill`: the average monthly bill the requirement rests on, in USD with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent.
- `required_amount`: the deposit amount required, in USD with 2 decimal places, a whole-dollar amount written with .00 cents.
- `first_installment_due_date`: the date the first (or only) installment is due, written YYYY-MM-DD as a calendar date with no time of day.

**Return.** A one-line text receipt naming the new deposit reference number, the agreement, the deposit kind, the required amount and average monthly bill in USD with 2 decimal places, the status (assessed) and the first installment due date; the deposit reference number in the receipt confirms the deposit was assessed.

title: Required Security Deposit on a Pending New Agreement
content:
**Clause.** The Security Deposit required on a new agreement still pending start is the deposit multiple of its kind times the kind's default average monthly bill, rounded to the cent and then up to the next whole dollar, raised to the kind's minimum deposit and limited to its maximum deposit. The default average monthly bill so used is the average monthly bill recorded on the deposit.


## Worked examples (hypothetical kinds)

| Hypothetical kind's figures | Product | Rounded to the cent, then up to whole dollars | Within minimum and maximum? | Deposit required (USD) | Average monthly bill recorded (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multiple 2.0, default bill USD 310.00, minimum USD 250.00, maximum USD 5000.00 | 620.00 | 620 | Yes | 620.00 | 310.00 |
| Multiple 2.5, default bill USD 2400.00, minimum USD 1000.00, maximum USD 50000.00 | 6000.00 | 6000 | Yes | 6000.00 | 2400.00 |
| Multiple 2.0, default bill USD 45.30, minimum USD 100.00, maximum USD 600.00 | 90.60 | 91 | Below the minimum | 100.00 | 45.30 |

**Is the deposit required ever a figure with cents?** No. After rounding to the cent the amount is taken up to the next whole dollar, and the minimum and maximum are whole-dollar figures.

title: Disconnection Notices and the Business Security Deposit Multiple
content:
Disconnection notices raise the multiple applied to the recalculated requirement of a held business Security Deposit.

**Rule.** Two or more disconnection notices issued on the secured Electric Service Agreement in the 12 months ending on the recalculation date add 0.5 to the multiple; exactly one adds 0.25; none adds nothing.

| Disconnection notices on the secured agreement in the 12 months | Added to the multiple |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 0.5 |
| Exactly one | 0.25 |
| None | Nothing |

Each disconnection notice on the agreement's record counts as one, whether written or final; notices on the customer's other agreements are not counted.

## Cases (hypothetical notice histories)

- A written notice 4 months and a final notice 3 months before the recalculation date: two notices, 0.5 added.
- One written notice 11 months before the recalculation date: 0.25 added.
- One written notice 13 months before the recalculation date: outside the 12 months, nothing added.

title: Disconnection Notices and the New Agreement Security Deposit Plan
content:
Disconnection notices shorten the installment plan of a Security Deposit on a new agreement.

**Clause.** Two or more disconnection notices issued on any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements in the 12 months ending on the payment date take 2 installments off the plan; exactly one takes 1 off; none takes nothing off.

| Disconnection notices on any of the customer's agreements in the 12 months | Installments taken off |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 2 |
| Exactly one | 1 |
| None | Nothing |

Each notice on record, written or final, counts as one, and notices on every agreement of the customer are counted together.

## Cases (hypothetical notice histories)

- One written notice on the customer's old agreement 7 months before the payment date and one final notice on another agreement 2 months before: two notices, 2 installments off.
- One written notice 9 months before the payment date: 1 installment off.
- One written notice 14 months before the payment date: outside the 12 months, nothing off.

title: Security Deposit Holdings Across a Customer's Service Agreements
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold Security Deposits on several service agreements, one deposit per service agreement. A Security Deposit is assessed on a service agreement only when no other deposit on the same service agreement is in assessed or held status. A new trigger on an agreement that already carries a held deposit is handled by recalculation of that deposit, not by a second deposit.

The rule sets no maximum on the number of a customer's agreements that may each carry a deposit; the limit is one open deposit per agreement.

## Basis of judgement

- **What is checked**: the deposits on file for the same service agreement and their status, as the deposit records show them before the assessment is made. A customer's statement that no deposit exists does not replace the record.
- **Which object**: the service agreement the new deposit would secure. Deposits on the customer's other agreements do not engage this rule.
- **Open statuses**: assessed and held. A deposit in waived, refunded, applied to final bill or cancelled status on the same agreement does not count as open.

## Decision table

| Deposit already on the same service agreement | Does this rule allow a separate Security Deposit to be assessed on it? |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| One in assessed status | No |
| One in held status | No; a new trigger on that agreement is handled by recalculating the held deposit |
| One in waived, refunded, applied to final bill or cancelled status only | Yes, the one-open-deposit condition is met |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A business customer holds a Small Commercial Service Deposit on its Schedule GS agreement at one site and opens a new agreement at a second site. The second agreement carries no deposit, so the one-deposit-per-agreement condition is met for it.
